title: Eigenstack orbit law generalizes dilation to affine T(γ)
evidence: The general (affine) eigenstack law C073 invokes is ALREADY PROVEN axiom-clean in-tree: ArkLib/Data/CodingTheory/ProximityGap/MCAEigenstackOrbitLaw.lean proves `mcaEvent_eigenstack_iff` (bad set invariant under T(γ)=a⁻¹b+γ·a⁻¹c for u₀∘σ=a·u₀+b·u₁, u₁∘σ=c·u₁) and `orderOf_{le,dvd}_badScalarSet_card_of_eigenstack` (#bad = ε + N·ord(a⁻¹c)), all #print-axioms clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. So C073's 'general law' is correct. I then tested whether the generalization gives anything NEW for the prize, via exact-integer probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/C073_eigenstack_orbit_quantization.py at a PROPER-subgroup prime μ_16 ⊂ F_65537* (|F*|=65536=16·4096, dyadic 2-power cofactor). THREE clean results: (T1) over 100 (a,b,c) triples with b varied incl. nonzero shifts, the T-orbit SIZE always equals ord(a⁻¹c) INDEPENDENT of b — the affine 'generalization' is purely a fixed-point translation, the multiplicative quantum is the SAME ord(a⁻¹c) as the monomial ladder, adding NO new arithmetic. (T2) with the quantum d=ord(a⁻¹c) FIXED, ε_mca=#bad/q²=(ε+N·d)/q² scales LINEARLY in the orbit COUNT N, not in d; the orbit size d≤n≤2^m is the trivially-bounded factor, exactly matching DISPROOF_LOG Loop43/44/45 (literal prize ε_mca ≤ N·d/q, S=d≤2^m free, open core = orbit COUNT N = Q2/PolyOrbitCount). (T3) the KKH26 near-capacity bad line has ≥2^r·C(2^{μ-1},r) close scalars (exponential); dividing by the order-s quantum leaves orbit COUNT N=#bad/s STILL exponential (μ→μ+1 ratios 2.0–4.4 for r=2,3) — s-quantization shaves one factor s off an exponential, giving NO polynomial bound, fully consistent with KKH26's already-proven ceiling. Cross-check: EsymmFiber.lean's own `not_explainableCoreSupply_rootsOfUnity` independently proves the smooth-μ_n supply is exponential, so crossing the orbit law with the EsymmFiber count yields an exponential LOWER bound on the list, never a polynomial upper bound on N.
honest_note: The general affine eigenstack law and its ord(a⁻¹c)-divisibility ARE genuinely proven (in-tree, axiom-clean) — C073 is right that the law generalizes the dilation. What is OPEN/vacuous-for-prize is the prize-relevance: quantization caps only the orbit SIZE (the free factor d≤2^m), while the prize content is the orbit COUNT N, which after quantizing the KKH26 line remains exponential. The probe T2/T3 use the structural orbit-union model the in-tree law proves (T-invariant bad sets) and the KKH26 published #close lower bound; they do not enumerate full RS bad sets at the prize prime (infeasible), so they confirm the SCALING (count, not size) rather than re-deriving KKH26. Verdict not REFUTED: nothing C073 asserts is false — the generalization holds; it simply welds the prize-relevant residual back to the orbit-count wall the project already isolated.
wall: Orbit-count wall N (DISPROOF_LOG Loop43/44/45 PolyOrbitCount / Chai-Fan 2026/861 Q2), which is the BGK/Paley √-cancellation core: orbit-size quantization (ord(a⁻¹c)≤n≤2^m) is free; the open content is an n-uniform polynomial bound on the bad-orbit COUNT N below capacity.
